Visit note | 2025-08-18 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Abul Pramanik, 70, male. Mr. Pramanik reports he has no symptoms at all, but mentions his father had a heart attack at 55 and high cholesterol was found on a routine test. He works as a farmer, and this discovery was made on a pre-employment test in Khilgaon. He has Hypothyroidism. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath on exertion. On examination: LDL cholesterol 5.8 mmol/L, BP 122/85 mmHg, pulse 71 bpm, weight 80 kg. Heart sounds are normal and peripheral pulses are intact. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 10:30 AM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Mahbub Hasan, 28, male. Mr. Hasan attends for review regarding his ongoing symptoms of a racing heart, hating the heat, and losing weight despite eating well. He works as a tailor and first noticed his clothes became loose during a stay in Mirpur. He has no reported comorbidity. He denies tremors or visual disturbances. On examination: pulse 126 bpm, BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 57 kg. Thyroid is visibly enlarged and smooth. Assessment: Hyperthyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid excess tea and coffee and rest when the heart races. Follow-up in 4 weeks with thyroid function tests.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 11:00 AM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Imtiaz Hasan, 78, male. Mr. Hasan comes in for a review complaining of losing weight without trying, always feeling thirsty, and cuts that heal slowly. He is a retired civil servant, and these issues were found during a routine test before a trip to Kushtia. He has no other major comorbidity. He denies blurred vision or numbness in his feet. On examination: fasting glucose 8.7 mmol/L, BP 132/86 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 68 kg. Chest is clear and abdomen is soft. Assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to reduce rice portions and sweets, walk briskly 30 minutes five days a week, check fasting sugar twice weekly, and check the feet daily. Follow-up in 3 months with HbA1c.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 11:00 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Saiful Munshi, 47, male. Mr. Munshi returns for a review visit reporting tense muscles and feeling restless. He works as a call centre agent, and his worries have been much worse since a family business loss in Farmgate. He has no other medical comorbidity. He denies panic attacks or suicidal ideation. On examination: GAD-7 score 13, BP 113/86 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 67 kg. He appears anxious but oriented in time and place. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 11:30 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Jannatul Ahmed, 41, female. Mrs. Ahmed attends for follow-up, noting symptoms are worse with stress, along with cramping belly pain and bloating. She works as a ride-share driver, and her symptoms became much worse since starting a high-pressure job in Rangpur. She presents with urgent loose stools every morning with little pain. She has no comorbidity. On examination: pain score 3/10, BP 134/79 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 51 kg. Abdomen is tender in the lower quadrants without guarding. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 11:30 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Marium Matubbar, 20, female. Miss Matubbar returns for review regarding acne and irregular periods. She works as a garment factory worker and noticed these changes after a friend in Cumilla suggested testing. She has Hypothyroidism. She denies excessive facial hair growth or pelvic pain. On examination: BMI 27.7, BP 134/77 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 74 kg. Examination shows mild acne on the jawline. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 12:30 PM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Tariq Uddin, 48, male. Mr. Uddin attends for review complaining of getting breathless on the stairs, looking pale, and noticing brittle nails. He works as a tailor and noticed this after months of skipping lunch during long shifts in Mirpur. He has no other comorbidity. He denies chest pain or gastrointestinal bleeding. On examination: haemoglobin 9.0 g/dL, BP 116/82 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 54 kg. Conjunctivae are pale. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 12:30 PM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Samira Khatun, 39, female. Mrs. Khatun attends for her first visit complaining of itchy watery red eyes that are worse in certain seasons. She works as a call centre agent, and her symptoms started during the flowering season in Dhanmondi. She presents with stringy discharge and swollen eyelids with little itch. She has no comorbidity. On examination: visual acuity 6/12 in the left eye, BP 118/86 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 92 kg. Conjunctivae are injected with mild papillary reaction. Assessment: Allergic conjunctivitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid rubbing the eyes, use cool compresses, and wear sunglasses outdoors. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 03:00 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Chandana Nath, 65, female. Mrs. Nath comes in for a follow-up visit regarding her respiratory symptoms. She states that she experiences a tight chest in dust or cold air, along with coughing at night and audible wheezing. She works as a homemaker, and her trouble started after moving into a damp flat in Gazipur. She has no known comorbidity. She denies fever, weight loss, or persistent chest pain. On examination: SpO2 92%, BP 113/73 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 78 kg. Auscultation of the chest reveals widespread expiratory wheezes bilaterally, but no focal crepitations. Her heart sounds are normal with no added murmurs. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued for her chronic respiratory care. She was counselled on disease management and advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up is scheduled in 1 month to check her inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 03:00 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Parvez Hasan, 73, male. Mr. Hasan returns for review, reporting long hours of screen time and symptoms that are worse in air conditioning. He works as a madrasa teacher, and his eye fatigue has been worse since night shifts at a call centre in Tongi. He has Hypothyroidism. He denies severe eye pain or sudden vision loss. On examination: tear break-up time 7 seconds, BP 131/72 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 97 kg. Corneas show mild superficial punctate staining. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 04:00 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Tuhin Shikder, 43, male. Mr. Shikder attends for his first visit complaining of fever and sharp chest pain on breathing in. He works as a garment factory worker, and his illness started after a long cold boat trip near Mohammadpur. He has no chronic comorbidity. He denies night sweats or chronic cough prior to this episode. On examination: temperature 103.2°F, BP 122/82 mmHg, pulse 103 bpm, SpO2 91%, weight 94 kg. Bronchial breathing and dullness to percussion noted over the right lower zone. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids, and return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-08-18 04:30 PM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Jewel Mollah, 63, male. Mr. Mollah attends for a follow-up visit reporting breathlessness worse for several days and wheezing on walking. He works as a homemaker, and his condition worsened after a cold caught at a crowded market in Tejgaon. He has Bronchial asthma. He denies recent chest trauma or haemoptysis. On examination: SpO2 88%, BP 123/81 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 50 kg. Bilateral wheezes and prolonged expiration are noted. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 10:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Gautam Bose, 38, male. Mr. Bose attends for a review visit describing needing to lie in a dark room and light hurting his eyes during attacks. He works as an architect, and his attacks are triggered by skipping meals while travelling in Old Dhaka. He has Essential hypertension. He denies visual aura changes lasting over an hour or focal weakness. On examination: about 8 headache days a month, BP 140/94 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 59 kg. Neurological examination is unremarkable. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 11:00 AM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Champa Awal, 23, female. Ms. Awal attends her first visit reporting that she works indoors all day and suffers from muscle cramps and low energy. She works as a software developer, and she noticed this after working in a windowless office in Wari. She has Essential hypertension. She denies bone tenderness or numbness. On examination: vitamin D level 16 ng/mL, BP 142/88 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 53 kg. General physical examination is normal. Assessment: Vitamin D deficiency. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get 20 minutes of morning sunlight daily and eat eggs and fish. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat vitamin D level.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 11:30 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Dipali Mitra, 76, female. Mrs. Mitra comes in for her first visit with a cough producing yellow or green sputum and sharp chest pain on breathing in. She is a madrasa teacher, and her illness began a week after a flu-like illness in Old Dhaka. She has no chronic comorbidity. She denies recent weight loss or night sweats. On examination: temperature 101.9°F, BP 130/78 mmHg, pulse 98 bpm, SpO2 93%, weight 61 kg. Crackles are heard over the left lung base. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids and return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 11:30 AM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Rupa Khatun, 35, female. Mrs. Khatun attends her first visit complaining of a blocked nose and thick nasal discharge for over ten days. She works as a restaurant cook, and her trouble started after a cold during a rainy week in Sirajganj. She has no comorbidity. She denies facial pain or dental ache. On examination: temperature 100.7°F, BP 121/71 mmHg, pulse 97 bpm, weight 86 kg. Nasal mucosa is congested with purulent secretions. Assessment: Acute sinusitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use steam inhalation twice daily and drink warm fluids. Follow-up in 10 days.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 02:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Marium Shikder, 21, female. Ms. Shikder attends her first visit with pain that wakes her at night and gnawing pain in her upper belly. She works as a schoolteacher, and her symptoms started after irregular meals on night shifts in Bogura. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies vomiting blood or black tarry stools. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 134/72 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 48 kg. Epigastric tenderness is present without rigidity. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 02:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Shapla Sultana, 62, female. Mrs. Sultana attends her first visit with a ring-shaped itchy red rash and an itch that is worse in humid weather. She works as a restaurant cook, and her rash started after playing football on wet fields in Savar. She has no comorbidity. She denies blistering or mucosal lesions. On examination: affected area about 2 cm across, BP 130/84 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 64 kg. Annular erythematous plaque with raised scaly borders on the forearm. Assessment: Tinea corporis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep the skin dry, not share towels, and wash clothes in hot water. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 03:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Mitu Khatun, 29, female. Mrs. Khatun attends her first visit complaining of pain behind her eyes, a sudden high fever, and severe aching in her bones and muscles. She works as a fisherman, and her illness began after a neighbour in Mymensingh was admitted with dengue. She has no comorbidity. She denies bleeding manifestations or shortness of breath. On examination: platelet count 61000 per microlitre, temperature 101.4°F, BP 110/77 mmHg, pulse 105 bpm, weight 86 kg. Mild petechiae noted on the lower limbs. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 03:00 PM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Salma Mahmud, 80, female. Mrs. Mahmud attends a follow-up visit reporting occasional dizziness and no other complaints. She works as a madrasa teacher, and her elevated reading was picked up at a pharmacy in Farmgate while buying other medicines. She has no other chronic comorbidity. She denies chest pain, syncope, or visual blurring. On examination: BP 154/102 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 90 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no murmurs. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 03:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tariq Shikder, 72, male. Mr. Shikder attends his first visit reporting a sour taste in his mouth and burning behind his breastbone after meals. He works as a tailor, and his symptoms have been worse since a job change in Motijheel meant late heavy dinners. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Visit note | 2025-08-19 03:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Monir Hasan, 38, male. Visit note | 2025-08-19 03:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Parvin Munshi, 22, female. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stay gently active, use a warm compress, and lift with the knees bent. Follow-up in 2 weeks if the pain continues.

Visit note | 2025-08-19 03:30 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Mamun Khan, 53, male. Visit note | 2025-08-19 03:30 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Farhan Khan, 51, male.
